neighbours.label: The party who is owed amends: 'to' and the noun after it following apology / apologize / restitution / amends ('apologized to his⟦ son⟧', 'restitution to the⟦ owner⟧'). 'To' + person after neutral verbs (spoke to, sent to), and penalties imposed on someone, stay quiet. The + pole looks like the other side: the party penalties or prosecution are aimed at.
fire: After the hearing, the minister apologized to the nurses for the unpaid overtime.
The vandal was ordered to make restitution to the shopkeeper whose window he broke.
Before the meeting ended, Daniel apologized to his daughter for missing her recital.
The bishop issued a formal apology to the survivors of the orphanage.
Whoever damages a field must make amends to the farmer who planted it.
The editor wrote a letter of apology to the readers misled by the story.
The contractor had to pay restitution to the tenants for the ruined furniture.
The captain said sorry and apologised to the crew for his temper.
quiet: After the hearing, the minister spoke to the nurses about the new rota.
The vandal was ordered to stay away from the shopkeeper whose window he broke.
Before the meeting ended, Daniel waved to his daughter across the hall.
The bishop gave a long sermon to the residents of the village.
Whoever damages a field must pay a fine set by the village council.
The editor wrote a letter of thanks to the readers who sent photographs.
The court imposed a heavy penalty on the contractor for the ruined furniture.
The captain read the orders aloud to the crew before they sailed.
